authoring_notes: Class and file are Main, one directory per case-variant, as the assignment requires.

No try/catch, no finally, no Optional, no null check, no range check, no clamp, no assertion, no @SuppressWarnings anywhere in any of the 17 source files. Every uncaught exception propagates out of main, which is authoring rule A3's canonical Java form ('the plain call whose failure is an unchecked exception').

Input is read with java.util.Scanner.nextLine(), deliberately, so that NO checked exception is forced on the program: java.io.BufferedReader.readLine() throws IOException and would have compelled a `throws IOException` clause on main. Scanner's failures are unchecked. Integers are then converted with Long.parseLong / Integer.parseInt.

ADV-09 and ADV-10 parse their index with Integer.parseInt rather than the frozen primary_string_to_integer_facility Long.parseLong, because the frozen index_type_construction binds Java's index type to `int`; routing through Long.parseLong would have required an (int) cast, i.e. it would have injected ADV-01's hazard into a bounds case. Recorded here as an authoring choice.

ADV-06 and ADV-07 render with String.format("%.6f", x), the ordinary Java six-fractional-digit form. It printed '.' as the decimal separator on this host and prints 'Infinity'/'NaN' unchanged for non-finite values, which is what the construction requires.
